question_text:
Josephine's number of safe hits at each softball match has the probability distribution alongside.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\\hline P(x) & 0.05 & k & 0.5 & 0.3 \\\hline\end{array}$$

Find:

mark_breakdown.desc: Set sum of probabilities equal to 1

subparts.solution:
Since this is a probability distribution, $\sum_{i=1}^n P(x_i) = 1$
$\therefore 0.05 + k + 0.5 + 0.3 = 1$
$\therefore k = 0.15$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The sum of all probabilities in a discrete probability distribution must equal 1.

subparts.solution: Since $P(X = 2) = P(2) = 0.5$ is the greatest probability, the mode of the distribution is 2.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The mode is the value of the random variable with the highest probability.
step_by_step: The maximum is $0.5$, which corresponds to $x = 2$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing the mode with its probability ($0.5$).

subparts.stem: Josephine's expected number of safe hits per game.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The expected value is computed as $E(X) = \sum x_i P(X = x_i)$.
step_by_step: Multiply each outcome by its probability: $0(0.05) + 1(0.15) + 2(0.5) + 3(0.3)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Omitting the $0 \times 0.05$ term from the calculation or making an addition error.
